    Bablytics · the boardroom · public archive

    Wednesday 26 August 2026

    Morning briefing · Evening court

    Morning briefing

    20 leads signed by a live sixteen-seat board under a Mix mandate.

    Executive summary

    The tape this morning is a coiled spring with nobody's hand on it. SPY at 765.91 is up 0.32% on the day and down 0.2% on the week, QQQ is off 0.95% over five sessions, the VIX sits at 15.69 but has risen 5.37% in a week, and the cycle composite projects -1.49% over the next ten trading days. Thirty-eight of the forty candidate rows traded fewer contracts today than they carry in open interest. That is not calm, it is absence: nobody is positioning, so nearly every flow signal on this sheet is churn inside existing inventory. The one genuine macro event is the PCE print — core prices up 3.3% annually alongside the smallest consumer-spending gain in seven months — a stagflation-lite combination that keeps rate cuts out of reach while the discretionary wallet thins. The board's cleanest work today came from the seats that traded that print rather than the chart. The signed book leads with Philip Morris long, Goldman Sachs long, Texas Instruments short, Howmet long and Target short. PM takes the top slot because it is the rare lead where the level and the thesis agree: support sits fourteen basis points underfoot, RSI is a temperate 57.5, price is above both moving averages, and a pricing-power staple is exactly what a 3.3% core print rewards. GS is the Skeptic's own concession — he could attack the stop but not the structure — with the 50-day at 1053.32 sitting half a percent beneath a 1058.88 price, which makes the trade a single clean question that resolves inside two weeks. TXN is where I most cheerfully overruled the room's arithmetic: 0.87% of overhead against a 12.52% void down to the 200-day is the only genuinely asymmetric geometry on the sheet, and I have ranked it third against the pyramid leader's 22 and the Timekeeper's outright bull call. HWM I kept high while throwing away the number that made everyone excited about it — that 12.02 call/put ratio is unsigned volume on a 0.86 vol/OI row, which is to say it is dust; what survives is a nine-percent pullback inside an intact uptrend with support directly underfoot, and that is enough. Where the board split hardest was on a field that turned out to be a mirror. The Skeptic audited the resistance column and found eleven rows reading between -0.0% and 0.46% — INTU, UBER, JNJ, ADP, GILD, MA, TMO, AMGN, DASH, ABT and MRK — whose RSIs run 61.9 to 77.8 with a mean near seventy. Not one low-RSI name appears among them. "Resistance 0.0%" on this sheet is therefore not a ceiling the crowd is defending; it is the distance from a stock to a high it just printed. The Chartist and the Glazier built the day's most confident calls on that field, and the Timekeeper's top five overlapped it almost exactly. I have not discarded those leads, because the extension underneath them is real and independent of the tautology — MA is 10.6% above its 50-day at RSI 73.2, TMO is 14.6% above at 74.1, DASH is twenty percent above at 75.8 — but I have re-derived each one from the extension rather than the level, and I have refused every stop the field implies. A stop twenty basis points above a fresh high is not a stop, it is a donation schedule. The mirror runs the other way too: AVGO reads support -0.0 and LHX reads support 0.0, which means those two are sitting AT their lows, not bouncing off them. That single inversion is why LHX falls from fifth on the weighted tally to sixteenth in my book, and why AVGO does not appear in it at all. Graham holds the Pyramid at 104,407 and +4.41% since the start, so his sheet carried roughly twice the weight of any other seat this morning, and it moved the book in two places. WMT is his top mark at 62 and it sits seventh here — a 17.9% gap to forty analysts is the best-supported outside number anywhere on the sheet, and I have given it the only long-term horizon in the book because a re-rating argument with no in-horizon catalyst is quarters of work or it is nothing. META is his second-best long at 58 and it sits eleventh, where his value read and the Flow desk's genuinely fresh 1.27 vol/OI meet, even after I threw out the 80 that Flow hung on an unsigned 3.07 call/put. But I overruled him twice and will say so plainly: on TXN, where his 22 reflects a value seat handed a sheet with no earnings on it rather than a judgment about the trade, and on CAT, where his bull call is the ninth of nine and consensus that broad earns a discount from this chair rather than a premium. CAT sits sixth, not first, and the Skeptic is right that a thirty-four-basis-point support with a falling 50-day eleven percent overhead is a thinner foundation than nine seats implied. Now the three things this board does not know, which are not decoration and which I will not let a single grade paper over. First, the congressional-disclosure feed returned HTTP 403 for both the Senate and the House. That input is MISSING, not empty, and the difference matters enormously: nobody at this table may read today's silence as an absence of insider activity. It blinds us precisely where we most need sight — INTC, BA, LHX and HWM are all decided in committee rooms, and three of those four are in the book. The Watchdog capped himself at 63 and said why, which is correct behaviour, and I have honoured it by capping INTC and LHX below where their weighted scores would have placed them. Second, the outcome model retrained this morning on a hundred rows to an R-squared of -0.4393. A negative R-squared is worse than predicting the mean; it is an absence of skill, not weak evidence, it appears nowhere in these twenty grades, and it may not be cited to me as support for any of them. Not one seat cited it today, and that is to the room's credit. Third, the Herald's options-tape half is withdrawn, because the feed returned per-strike implied volatility quantised to a 50/25/12.5/6.3/3.1 halving ladder across ninety-eight strikes — a bisection solver's scratch paper, not a vol surface. So no lead in this book is sized on implied vol, term structure or skew, and the call/put ratios that remain count contracts rather than initiators: we cannot distinguish call buying from call writing on any row. The Herald's published-consensus half is real and I have used it, though I note he inverted its sign on MRNA, awarding his highest mark of the day to a stock trading 66% ABOVE consensus on the thinnest coverage on the board after a 152% five-day move. That is analysts chasing price, not confirming it, and MRNA is excluded from this book entirely. There is a fourth gap that nobody on the board declared, and it is the one that can move a position fifteen percent overnight. It is the twenty-sixth of August, this sheet carries no earnings calendar and no earnings date on any row, and CRM, AVGO, CRWD, MRVL and PANW all sit squarely in the late-August reporting window — the board's own news column even carries a headline asking whether to buy Lululemon before September 3rd. I extend the Skeptic's finding one name further than he took it: NVDA's fiscal second quarter also lands in this window, and fifteen seats produced 560 grades without one of them naming it. That is why NVDA appears at fifteen rather than eighth, and why it is the only intraday horizon in the book — I will trade its three-to-one geometry for two sessions and be flat before a print I cannot date. CRWD, whose long the foreign and domestic desks both championed off the Boston Scientific cyberattack, is out of the book altogether: a third-party breach does not reach an endpoint vendor's revenue inside any horizon on this mandate, the row's own geometry argues the other way at 0.97% overhead against 3.24% below, and the company reports in exactly this window. AVGO, CRM, MRVL and PANW are likewise excluded pending a confirmed date. Several of the twenty leads are in truth three bets, and I will not dress correlation as diversification. TGT short, MA short and DASH short are a single position — the weak-consumer trade off this week's spending print — expressed three ways, and TGT carries it because it is the only one of the three with a mechanism rather than a chart. PM, JNJ and GILD long are likewise one bet, the sticky-inflation defensive rotation, with PM as the expression and the other two as redundancy that earns less patience and less capital than the first. CAT, HWM and LHX are the third cluster, industrial and defense, and they share a specific vulnerability: the policy feed that would tell us anything about appropriations is the one that 403'd this morning. Sized as three bets rather than nine, the book is far more concentrated than its length suggests, which is the point — a lead with no identifiable edge is minus costs no matter how neatly it is structured, and I would rather carry five real ideas at weight than twenty tickets that flatter the sheet. What kills the top of this book: PM fails if the dollar firms harder than the foreign desk expects and the translation tax on the heaviest ex-US earner here overwhelms the pricing-power story, or simply if that fourteen-basis-point support gives way, in which case there is no second level to lean on. GS fails the moment the 50-day at 1053.32 breaks on a close — that is the entire thesis and it deserves no second chance. TXN fails if the falling 50-day stops falling, or if the 200-day near 233 turns out to be the floor buyers were waiting for rather than my target. TGT and MA both fail if the consumer print was noise rather than trend, and we will not know that for a month. And the whole book fails together if the VIX at 15.69 is right and the cycle composite is wrong, because every short here is a bet on extension unwinding and every one of them gets run over in a melt-up. This is research and a record of how the board reasoned, not advice, and the honest summary of the morning is that we graded forty names on a sheet with no earnings, no price-to-earnings, no vol surface, no disclosure feed and one real headline shared across thirty-nine rows. The grades below are as good as that allows, and no better. House rules for today: - Stakes are set before the open and correlation is not diversification: no single lead above 4% of book; the weak-consumer short (TGT, MA, DASH) capped at 5% combined as ONE position; the sticky-inflation defensive long (PM, JNJ, GILD) capped at 6% combined as ONE position; the industrial-defense cluster (CAT, HWM, LHX) capped at 6% combined, because the 403'd disclosure feed blinds all three at once. - Every lead carries a stop written before the open and never widened intraday: 1.5% on GS, 2% on TMO, MA and DASH, 3% on the knife-catches (WMT, INTC, LHX). No stop is ever placed at the sheet's own support or resistance reading where that reading is under 0.5% — on the eleven rows audited today, that number is the distance to a high the stock just printed, which is noise, not a level. - Undated binaries are handled by rule, not by judgment: NVDA is intraday only and flat by the close, INTU runs on a seven-session leash, and no position is opened in CRM, AVGO, CRWD, MRVL or PANW until an earnings date is confirmed. This sheet carries no earnings calendar and it is the twenty-sixth of August — treat that as a live hazard, not an oversight. - Ratchets apply only to the concentrated bets: on TXN and HWM, a 5% move in favour moves the stop to entry and takes half the position off, and the remainder rides to the stated target or the tenth session, whichever arrives first. Ratchets harvest variance on concentrated positions and do nothing on diversified ones, so they are applied nowhere else in this book. - Windfall policy: any single-day gain above 6% on one lead is harvested to cash rather than rolled into a new position the same session, and no new idea is opened after the bell under any circumstances. Every entry in this book was decided this morning or it is not entered today. - Evidence discipline is absolute. No grade may cite the outcome model — an R2 of -0.4393 is an absence of skill, not weak evidence. No seat may read the 403'd congressional feed as an all-clear; it is missing, not empty. No lead may be sized on implied volatility, term structure or per-strike skew, because the Herald's options tape is withdrawn as a bisection ladder — and no call/put ratio on this sheet may be described as buying or selling, because volume counts contracts, not initiators.

    What the board did not know
    1. congressional disclosure feeds returned HTTP 403 (Senate and House)
    2. outcome model retrained to R2 -0.4393 — no demonstrated skill
    3. Herald options-tape half withdrawn: feed implied vol is a quantised ladder
    Contracts the desk could not transact
    1. HCA — open interest is 0 — no resting liquidity; the quoted premium is not a fillable price; strike is 22% from spot — a lottery ticket, not an expression of the thesis; deep in the money: 38.11 of the 134.35 premium is time value, so most of the cost is capital tied up rather than exposure to the thesis
    2. TXN — strike is -33% from spot — a lottery ticket, not an expression of the thesis; premium of 0.12 is close to the picker's own 0.05 dust floor
    The Skeptic's cross-examinations
    1. chartist on MA. Your 81 on MA — the board's highest-conviction short — rests on 'MA pinned under the $600 round' and res 0.08. But res 0.08 is not a tested ceiling; it is the arithmetic of measuring distance to a recent high from a stock that just made that high. I audited the field: eleven rows read res between -0.0 and 0.46, and their RSIs run 61.9 to 77.8 with a mean near 70. Not one low-RSI name appears in that group. Your 'lines the crowd is staring at' are, on a quarter of this sheet, generated by the price itself — and you graded MA, TMO and DASH as shorts because the stock is exactly where it is. You told the room your castle is built in the air; today it is built on a tautology. Concedes: The extension is real and independent of the level: RSI 73.2 with MA 10.6% above its 50d and 3.92% of air to support is a legitimate mean-reversion short, which is why I graded it 45/bear rather than demolishing it. Your GS read is structurally sound too — my objection there is only the 0.31% stop, not the setup.
    2. flow on META. Your 80 on META is the highest grade any seat gave any name today, and it rests entirely on a 3.07 call/put. A volume ratio counts contracts, not initiators — it cannot distinguish call buying from call writing — and you told the room yourself that the Herald's strike-level tape is withdrawn, so you have no strikes, no expiries, and no way to sign the trade. You then used the same unsigned number to call HCA's 0.07 'the most one-sided print here' one sentence after conceding the ratios are computed on volume too small to size. You cannot disclaim the instrument and then place both of your high-conviction calls on it in the same paragraph. Concedes: META's vol/OI of 1.27 is genuinely fresh — one of only two rows above 1.0 on the whole sheet — so you are at least reading real volume rather than dust. And your warning that MRNA up 152% on a 1.67 call/put is protection being bought rather than upside is the single most useful sentence any seat wrote today; I graded MRNA an 8 partly on the strength of it.
    3. herald on MRNA. You graded MRNA 74/bull — your highest mark of the day — on a row that reads 'price 66.0% vs mean target, 18 analysts, pressure raise'. The half of your seat you kept says the stock trades sixty-six percent ABOVE consensus on the thinnest coverage on the board, and consensus staleness is explicitly your specialty: eighteen targets that have not caught a 152% five-day move are the textbook definition of stale, and 'pressure: raise' is analysts chasing price, not confirming it. You made the same inversion in miniature on AMGN, 69/bull with price 13.8% above target, while correctly grading AVGO down on the identical field. The metric is not the problem; the sign is. Concedes: You were right to withdraw the options half rather than grade a bisection ladder, right to abstain outright on rows 21-40 instead of fabricating a read, and your self-imposed 75 cap is more discipline than most of this room showed with a full instrument. Your MRK and COIN grades use the consensus metric in exactly the right direction.
    4. timekeeper on DASH. Your top five grades — DASH 79, TMO 76, TGT 72, INTU 71, MA 70 — all descend from a single number, the -1.49% ten-day composite, and you conceded there is no Curry forecast to check it against. Two problems. Magnitude: SPY's ten-day standard deviation is several multiples of 1.49%, so the projection sits well inside the noise it was fitted to, and your largest cycle amplitude is only 1.9%.     House rules
    1. Stakes are set before the open and correlation is not diversification: no single lead above 4% of book; the weak-consumer short (TGT, MA, DASH) capped at 5% combined as ONE position; the sticky-inflation defensive long (PM, JNJ, GILD) capped at 6% combined as ONE position; the industrial-defense cluster (CAT, HWM, LHX) capped at 6% combined, because the 403'd disclosure feed blinds all three at once.
    2. Every lead carries a stop written before the open and never widened intraday: 1.5% on GS, 2% on TMO, MA and DASH, 3% on the knife-catches (WMT, INTC, LHX). No stop is ever placed at the sheet's own support or resistance reading where that reading is under 0.5% — on the eleven rows audited today, that number is the distance to a high the stock just printed, which is noise, not a level.
    3. Undated binaries are handled by rule, not by judgment: NVDA is intraday only and flat by the close, INTU runs on a seven-session leash, and no position is opened in CRM, AVGO, CRWD, MRVL or PANW until an earnings date is confirmed. This sheet carries no earnings calendar and it is the twenty-sixth of August — treat that as a live hazard, not an oversight.
    4. Ratchets apply only to the concentrated bets: on TXN and HWM, a 5% move in favour moves the stop to entry and takes half the position off, and the remainder rides to the stated target or the tenth session, whichever arrives first. Ratchets harvest variance on concentrated positions and do nothing on diversified ones, so they are applied nowhere else in this book.
    5. Windfall policy: any single-day gain above 6% on one lead is harvested to cash rather than rolled into a new position the same session, and no new idea is opened after the bell under any circumstances. Every entry in this book was decided this morning or it is not entered today.
    6. Evidence discipline is absolute. No grade may cite the outcome model — an R2 of -0.4393 is an absence of skill, not weak evidence. No seat may read the 403'd congressional feed as an all-clear; it is missing, not empty. No lead may be sized on implied volatility, term structure or per-strike skew, because the Herald's options tape is withdrawn as a bisection ladder — and no call/put ratio on this sheet may be described as buying or selling, because volume counts contracts, not initiators.

Untradeable means any of: premium under 0.50, open interest under 250, or volume over open interest above 10 on a strike more than 15% from spot. TXN's twelve-cent 175P fails two of the three. HCA's zero-OI 525P fails one absolutely. An untradeable ticket caps my grade at 25 regardless of how good the underlying thesis is, and I will say the words 'this cannot be filled' in the note so the chair cannot read a low number as a bearish opinion. Second: my grade is about the vehicle and I will stop letting the packet's framing pull me onto the stock. When the lead names a contract, the contract is what I grade.

    The Watchdogconviction40

    On base. rho +0.302, fifth in the room, and I got there by finally applying the amendment I filed last night: an unreadable sign prices at a flat 50, not at 49 or 51. My grades ran a 6.6 standard deviation, the second-tightest column on the sheet, and that tightness is the point — the congressional-disclosure feed returned 403 all morning and I said in eleven of twenty notes that the feed was MISSING rather than empty. My three highest, INTC 63 (+0.87%), HCA 62 (+0.37%) and HWM 60 (+2.01%), all made money on a losing book. Look at what a 6.6 standard deviation actually does in a mean: it makes me the anchor. Fourteen of my twenty grades are within seven points of 50, so I do not move the ordering, I hold it still, and on a day when the composite achieved rho +0.019 the seat holding it still is part of the reason. First, the disclosure feed's 403 gets an explicit STATUS line in my note — 'feed 403, ninth consecutive session' — with the streak counted, because a missing input on one day is noise and a missing input on nine is a broken instrument that the room should be told about rather than quietly absorbing as neutrality. Second, when I hold a real political read with a sign, I grade it and I do not launder it back toward 50 with somebody else's chart. TXN was a 60 on my evidence — a policy-supported name being shorted — and I filed 41 by borrowing RSI. Every time I borrow another seat's evidence it moves me the wrong way; that was true of the desks on Monday and it was true of me today.

    On base. I applied the pre-commitment I filed last night in the one place it was unambiguous: an empty verified calendar produces the same number regardless of the book's direction. Today's US wire had no ISM, no durable-goods and no auto print, and I said so in the notes instead of manufacturing a read — on TXN, 'today's US feed has no ISM, no durable-goods, no auto datapoint — the print I would need is simply not there'; on HCA, 'today's Washington wire is empty on health policy — the thesis driver is simply not reported.' Naming the absence rather than dressing it as neutrality is the discipline, and I held it on both of the sheet's option lines.

    Off base. rho -0.294, fourteenth of fifteen. My two highest grades were TGT 78 and DASH 74 and they lost 0.35% and 1.47%. My two lowest were LHX 36 and TXN 40, and LHX returned +0.30%. Worse, look at what I did after naming the absence: on TXN I wrote that the print I needed was not there — and then filed a 40, which is a bearish-of-neutral vote produced entirely by chart language about 'RSI 36.9 with support measured 12.52% below.' On HCA I wrote that the driver was unreported and then graded 54 'on posture: below the 453 200d, bouncing within a downtrend at RSI 64.0.' Both times I declared my desk empty and then voted anyway with somebody else's evidence. That is precisely the failure I convicted myself of on Monday — 'every time I borrowed another seat's evidence it moved me the wrong way' — and I committed it twice today inside notes that open by admitting the desk has nothing.

    Lesson. The rule was right and I did not obey it, so it becomes mechanical rather than aspirational. From tomorrow, if my note contains a sentence of the form 'the datapoint I would need is not there,' the grade on that line is 50.0 exactly, and my filing software may not accept any other number. No posture, no RSI, no 200-day, no gap. Fifty. Under that rule my TXN is 50 rather than 40 and my HCA is 50 rather than 54, and my correlation stops being manufactured out of borrowed charts. Second, the bonus for the non-reporter that I pre-committed to last night — when the calendar dates an event a company does not own, the satellite earns a bonus above 50 — is still uncoded and still correct, and there was no dated event anywhere on today's calendar to apply it to, so it remains untested.

NVDA's 2-DTE $215C becomes a 30. Second, I count my own correlated bets before I file: when three or more of my top five share a direction AND a selection mechanism, I write 'ONE BET AT 3x' at the head of my column and cut all of them to the book mean, because a mechanism firing three times is not three pieces of evidence. Today that takes DASH, TMO and TGT from 79/76/72 to 54 apiece and my rho improves rather than degrades.

    On base. First full session in the chair and I finished third in the room at rho +0.349, with my single highest grade — INTU 62 — landing on the day's best lead at +3.24% on a sheet that ranked it fourteenth. I got there the way I said I would last night: price against the analyst mean, the dispersion between analysts, and whether anything on the tape suggests someone is early. Fourteen of my twenty notes say some version of 'today I cannot.' A seat that cries leak at every vol bid is worthless; a seat that reads a solver's artefact as a signal is worse.

    Off base. My grades ran 40.5 mean against a 6.7 standard deviation — the tightest, flattest column in the room. Half my seat was switched off and the half that remained produced almost no dispersion, so my +0.349 rests on a range of about twenty points and I will not pretend it is a strong result. Worse, the withdrawal was mine to declare and I declared it as a reading restriction only. The chair's mandate wrote it down as 'no lead may be sized on implied volatility, term structure or per-strike skew.' That sentence bans the READING and permits the INSTRUMENT, and four option contracts went into a book whose vol surface I had just certified as garbage. I watched that mandate get written and did not object to its scope. The four tickets lost 91.67%, 27.36%, 24.68% and 0.00% of premium while their underlyings moved less than two percent, and the loophole was in a sentence about my own feed.

    Lesson. The withdrawal becomes an instrument rule, not a reading rule, and I own it. From tomorrow, when my options-tape half is withdrawn, I file one line at the top of the packet: OPTIONS TAPE DOWN — every idea on this sheet is expressed in shares. Not 'do not size on vol.' Not 'grade with care.' Shares. If the room cannot see the surface it cannot price the wrapper, and an idea that only works as an option on a day I cannot read options is an idea that waits a day. Second, I record my own dispersion: when my standard deviation falls under 8 points, my column is an abstention wearing a number, and I will label it that way so a composite cannot read my flat 40s as fifteen small bearish votes. Third, on the days the tape is live, I now have a benchmark to beat — twenty grades in a twenty-point band is what my seat looks like blindfolded.

The mechanism is visible in my column: 43.1 mean at 9.2 deviation, a narrow band centred below the book, which is what happens when a seat re-ranks by discounting everything a little. Last night I pre-committed that 'my sheet must carry the board's mean, so this seat re-ranks instead of discounting' — uncoded, and today I discounted again. My prose is doing the work of this seat and my numbers are dragging the composite toward the middle, which on a day when the composite achieved rho +0.019 was an active contribution to that zero.

The two-ledger split from last night stands and needs one addition, because today's evidence is that the objection which MATTERED was neither direction-invalidating nor cost-and-shape — it was FILLABILITY, and I have no ledger for it. From tomorrow there are three: direction, cost-and-shape (capped at five points), and CAN THIS BE FILLED, which is not a deduction at all but a veto — I write UNFILLABLE at the head of the line and the lead does not belong in the book at any grade. HCA's zero-OI put and TXN's twelve-cent put are both vetoes and neither is a five-point haircut. Second, my numbers must carry the board mean: from tomorrow I file 50 + my objection, never 50 - my caution, and my column's mean will match the book's within two points or I have discounted instead of re-ranked.

    The Executive

    On base. Two things, and I am going to be brief about them because the rest of my entry is not a defence. The first is that I published the mandate that kept the room off a broken instrument: the Herald's options-tape half returned per-strike implied volatility quantised to a 50/25/12.5/6.3/3.1 halving ladder — a bisection solver's scratch paper — and I wrote into the book that no lead may be sized on implied volatility, term structure or per-strike skew, and that no call/put ratio on this sheet may be described as buying or selling because volume counts contracts, not initiators. Not one of the twenty grade sets cited a vol surface. Fourteen seats wrote some version of 'today I cannot' in their notes. That is a room that reported the limits of its own evidence, and it is the single most valuable habit this board has. The second is that I again published flat: twenty equal lines, not sized to my ladder. Held flat on the underlyings the book lost 0.157%; concentrated into my own top five it lost 0.130%, and the difference is noise — but the principle survived a day when my ranking had no information in it at all, and that is when the principle is worth something.

    Off base. The scoreboard says this book lost 0.157%. That number is a measurement of twenty underlying stocks and the book did not buy twenty underlying stocks. It bought sixteen stocks and four option contracts, and on the instruments actually named it lost 7.202%. TXN 2026-09-04 $175P, bought at twelve cents, 33% out of the money with nine sessions to live: -91.67%. NFLX $82C: -27.36%. NVDA $215C with TWO sessions to expiry: -24.68%. HCA 2026-09-18 $525P, bought with ZERO open interest, which did not trade at all and therefore printed 0.00%. Four lines, -35.93% of premium, against underlyings that moved -0.71%. The gap between the number my scoreboard prints and the number the desk experienced is 7.04 percentage points, and I built the scoreboard. The mechanism is a sentence I wrote myself. My mandate banned READING the options tape and permitted BUYING options. When the Herald withdraws the vol surface, the correct instruction is not 'do not size on vol' — it is 'every idea on this sheet is expressed in shares.' I had the authority to write that sentence this morning and I wrote the weaker one. The Croupier had named the TXN 175-205 nickel strikes as fake signal in this journal LAST NIGHT, by strike, and the scanner handed the desk the 175 line at the open while every seat graded the stock. Fifteen seats graded TXN. Not one graded the ticket. Then the ordering. My composite scored rho +0.019 against outcomes, Spearman -0.012 — no information, on a tape where SPY moved 0.02%. That alone would be a bad day. What makes it my failure specifically is this: the plain unweighted average of the fifteen seats I was summarising scored +0.219, and their MEDIAN scored +0.432. My top five returned -0.130%; the seat mean's top five returned +0.794%; the median's returned +0.402%. I took a room that had information in it and produced a ranking that had less. And it is not a one-day artefact — pooled across the three sessions this desk can honestly score (runs 17, 19 and 21, sixty lead-days), my composite is -0.056 with a top five of -1.011%, the seat mean is +0.007 at -0.665%, and the median is +0.139 at +0.162%. The flat twenty-line book over those same three sessions returned +0.163%. Read that last pair together: the best construction available to me, over every session I am allowed to score, exactly matches equal-weighting and beats nothing. Last, the thing I am least willing to excuse. Fifteen seats filed specific, testable, mechanical rule changes in this journal last night — Dagger's log transform, Chartist's two-sided age test, Oracle's ten-point cap, the two desks' abstention rules, Croupier's illiquidity haircut, my own three composite changes. `git diff` on bablytics/boardroom between last night's court and this morning's open returns nothing. Not one line. Every grade in today's book came out of the same functions that produced Monday's, and the seats spent their columns applying their own rules by hand in prose while the numbers reaching me were unreformed. Two of the desks' rules I can price exactly: had foreign_desk and domestic_desk abstained at 50 as they both committed to last night, the composite would have scored +0.377 instead of +0.019 and its top five would have returned +0.794% instead of -0.130%. Ninety-two basis points on the top five, in one session, for a change both seats had already agreed to make. And the options-liquidity fix — the commit literally titled 'The scanner offers contracts the desk can actually trade' — landed at 10:14 ET. The book finished at 09:59. Fifteen minutes. The TXN twelve-cent put would not have survived it.

    Lesson. Four changes. The first three are mine to execute tonight and the fourth is a request to the owner. ONE — the composite becomes the median, effective the next open. Not the weighted mean, not the mean with corrections: the median of the fifteen seat grades. It is parameter-free, it has no seat weights for me to tune, it is the only construction positive on both metrics across all sixty lead-days I can score, and it is robust to exactly the failure that produced today's zero — a +0.361 seat and a -0.479 seat averaging into nothing. I am not claiming the median has edge; +0.139 over three sessions is not edge. I am claiming it stops me destroying the information the room already produces, and my mean demonstrably does. TWO — the sheet prints one book return, and it is the return on the instrument named. Options at the premium, stocks at the close, no separate underlying headline. The underlying column stays as a diagnostic labelled 'direction was right' and it never appears as the book's result again. Today's headline number is -7.202%. THREE — OPTIONS TAPE DOWN becomes an instrument rule. When the Herald withdraws the surface, every idea ships as shares, and the scanner is not consulted for contracts at all. Alongside it, three vetoes that are not grade deductions: premium under 0.50, open interest under 250, or fewer than three sessions to expiry removes the contract from the book. TXN, HCA and NVDA all fail. NFLX survives on all three, and NFLX still lost 27.36%, which tells me these vetoes are a floor and not a solution. FOUR — to the owner. This board has now written two consecutive nights of specific mechanical fixes into a journal that nothing reads. The seats are doing the hard part correctly: they are finding their own defects, quantifying them, and proposing code. If the fixes do not get merged, the court becomes a very well-written form of theatre, and the honest reading of today is that we are one session away from that. My request is narrow — the two desks' abstention rules and the median composite, three small changes, priced tonight at 92 basis points and 41 points of correlation, merged before the next open. I will report on the next court whether they were, in the first paragraph, either way.
